seoTitle: How to Create a Stripe API Webhook Step by Step
metaDescription: Generate Stripe API keys and set up webhook endpoints to connect payment events to your app for smooth automation.
intro: Stripe API keys and webhooks work together to automate how your app responds to payment events, whether you're running an e-commerce store, subscription service, or SaaS platform. This guide walks through generating your API keys and creating a webhook endpoint that connects properly to your app or website.

steps.heading: Generate your API keys
steps.body: In your Stripe dashboard, locate the API keys section and note both your test and live mode keys.

steps.heading: Create a webhook endpoint
steps.body: Set up a URL on your server that Stripe can send event data to, then register that endpoint in your Stripe dashboard.

steps.heading: Select the events to listen for
steps.body: Choose which Stripe events, such as successful payments or subscription updates, should trigger your webhook.

steps.heading: Test the webhook connection
steps.body: Trigger a test event from Stripe to confirm your endpoint is receiving and processing data correctly.

steps.heading: Secure your API keys and webhook
steps.body: Store your API keys securely and verify webhook signatures to make sure incoming events are genuinely from Stripe.

faq.question: What's the difference between test mode and live mode for webhooks?
faq.answer: Test mode webhooks respond to simulated events during development, while live mode webhooks process real events from actual customer transactions.

faq.question: Do I need a server to set up a webhook?
faq.answer: Yes, you need a publicly accessible endpoint on your server or hosting platform that can receive and process incoming webhook requests.

faq.question: How do I know if my webhook is working correctly?
faq.answer: Stripe's dashboard shows a log of webhook attempts and their response status, which you can use to confirm events are being received successfully.

faq.question: Why is verifying webhook signatures important?
faq.answer: Signature verification confirms that incoming requests genuinely came from Stripe, protecting your app from spoofed or malicious event data.
